transcript:
[Meeting header]
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Aquila CTO), Liam O'Connor (SRE Lead), Sofia Reyes (ML Eng)

Summary: quick scoping for POC focused on capacity sizing and autoscale; target latency SLOs, reserved capacity + burst, fallback model options; next steps to run benchmarks and exchange traces.

Topics: success criteria, qps/rps, token counts per request, benchmark plan, reserved GPU sizing (A100 80GB), burst to hosted, fallback to quantized variant, network/VPC requirements, timeline for POC (3 weeks).

-- Transcript (timestamps are approximate, auto-generated) --
00:00 Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, I'll hand it over to Daniel for the technical walk, we have Priya, Liam and Sofia from Aquila, thanks for carving time.
00:12 Priya: hey thanks, um yeah excited to talk through how this POC could look like and to scope capacity, we've got a little backlog of use-cases but primar- primarily conversational summarization and code-assist.
00:25 Daniel: great, can you run us through the rough traffic profile — qps, token sizes, peak windows? even ballpark is fine.
00:32 Sofia: yeah sure — current is roughly 120 rps average across our API, peaks up to 450 rps in 5-min bursts. payloads vary, prompts avg ~350 tokens, responses avg ~220 tokens so total ~570 tokens per request. we also have some long job flows that go up to 3k tokens but that's <2% of traffic.
00:55 Liam: and latency's pretty sensitive — product wants 95th perc latency <1s for interactive flows.
01:03 Maya: ok got it; so success criteria we should pin are: 95p latency <1s, error rate <1% during peak, and cost targets — what's acceptable on cost per 1k requests?
01:18 Priya: ballpark we want cost to be lower than our current managed provider by at least 20% — otherwise VP will push back.
01:27 Daniel: understood. For POC we typically do reserved capacity for predictable throughput — e.g., reserve 2 GPUs (A100 80GB) as a baseline and allow burst to hosted pooled capacity for spikes. that gives deterministic latency for steady load and reduces cost compared to going all-hosted.
01:46 Priya: can you explain how burst to hosted pool works? like if our reserved are saturated will requests queue or fall back?
01:53 Daniel: yeah good question — our routing policy has a couple of options, you can either queue briefly with backpressure, or route excess to the hosted Redwood fleet which is multi-tenant. we also support automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model variant locally — lower perf but cheaper — or region fallback. so options: 1) burst to hosted, 2) fallback to quantized variant, 3) simple queue & reject policy.
02:17 Liam: we need security guarantees — if we burst to hosted multi-tenant, is data isolated? can we avoid sending PII?
02:25 Maya: important point — for the POC we can gate sensitive calls to only run on reserved private capacity; non-sensitive traffic can use burst. also we can anonymize or token-mask traces before sending to hosted. we'll also share SOC2 docs and the networking checklist.
02:39 Priya: ok good. about sizing: with 450 rps peaks and ~570 tokens/request, what does 2x A100 cover?
02:48 Daniel: rough math — an A100 80GB on our runtime for the model you mentioned (open-llm-ish 70B variant) gives about 18-22 rps for that token size with target latency under 1s, so 2 GPUs would give ~40-44 rps sustained. clearly not enough for 450 rps peaks. so reserved-only would be expensive. the typical approach is reserve for baseline load — say reserve for 150 rps steady, and rely on burst to hosted for the remaining peak, combined with autoscale rules to spin additional reserved nodes if average load stays high for N minutes.
03:20 Priya: hmm ok so what's a realistic POC config then?
03:24 Daniel: for POC we recommend reserving 2 GPUs to cover your steady baseline (we can size baseline from your 95th hour-by-hour), plus configure burst to hosted and an autoscale policy: scale out 1 additional GPU when 5-min avg >70% utilization for 10 minutes, with a max of +4 reserved for the POC. also enable fallback to quantized variant beyond max. that keeps cost bounded but shows behavior under load.
03:48 Sofia: what's the delta in latency/quality when falling back to quantized variant? some of our prompts are sensitive to hallucination risk.
03:55 Daniel: quantized 4-bit variants typically increase failure modes a bit — quality regression depends on prompt. we recommend running A/B benchmarks during POC to measure quality delta on your eval set; we also provide automatic quality monitoring to detect meangful regressions and rollback.
04:10 Priya: ok we'll definitely want the A/B. timeline-wise how long to run the POC?
04:16 Maya: we usually do a 3-week POC: week 0 (setup and trace exchange), week 1 run benchmarks & perf tuning, week 2 run production-like soak with traffic or replay, then a wrap & decision. we can compress if you need.
04:28 Liam: networking — do we need VPC peering or can we run via public endpoints? we prefer private for the production-like soak.
04:35 Daniel: for POC you can do VPC peering or use PrivateLink depending on cloud. we have a network checklist; if you want on-prem-ish isolation we can provision a private control plane. we'll include the exact steps in the checklist.
04:48 Priya: great. benchmarks — what's needed from us?
04:51 Daniel: ideally: 7 days of request traces, token length histograms, sample prompts, and your eval prompt set with expected outputs for quality checks. we'll run throughput tests using your samples and a representative concurrency profile; we'll measure 50/95/99 latencies, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
05:08 Sofia: we can provide that. for throughput tests do you use synthetic replay or live traffic?
05:13 Daniel: we do both: replay of anonymized traces for realistic patterns, and synthetic ramp tests to push extremes. for the replay we need request timestamps and token counts.
05:22 Priya: what about fallback policies? we want to avoid user-facing errors; prefer slower responses over errors.
05:28 Maya: yeah common policy is prefer fallback to quantized model or degrade to shorter responses rather than errors; also we can serve degraded content with a header to the app so you can surface a slightly different UX. we can configure per-route policies.
05:43 Liam: will the autoscale spin up GPUs fast enough to handle a 5-min spike?
05:47 Daniel: cold spin-up for reserved GPUs is a few minutes depending on instance type — H100 may be faster but cost is higher. that's why we suggest the burst to hosted pool for short spikes and autoscale for sustained increases. you can also pre-warm kernels for predicted events.
06:02 Priya: can you give a concrete example with numbers so execs understand?
06:06 Daniel: sure — example: baseline steady 150 rps -> reserve 2x A100 (covers ~40 rps each at our model profile, so ~80 rps usable, you might need 3 GPUs to reach 150 rps actually). okay adjust: reserve 3x A100 to cover baseline 150 rps. configure burst to hosted for up to 400 rps extra; autoscale adds up to +4 reserved GPUs if 10-min avg stays high. approximate POC monthly cost estimate will vary but we'll provide per-hour pricing in the quote.
06:38 Maya: note I'll include a cost comparison: pure-hosted vs reserved+burst vs dedicated private for full production.
06:46 Priya: and what's the rollback plan if quality drops during an autoscale event?
06:50 Daniel: we tie quality monitoring to your eval set; if regression crosses threshold we auto-failover to the previous stable model and roll back autoscale policy; alerting goes to Slack/email.
06:59 Sofia: sounds good. any required IAM/SAML steps?
07:02 Maya: we'll send an onboarding checklist — SSO for console access, RBAC roles for engineers, and the service account keys for the POC.
07:10 Priya: ok next steps then — we'll share traces by end of friday, and we want the benchmark run early next week.
07:18 Maya: great we'll schedule the benchmark for wk of 2026-12-13. I'll share the SOC2 link and the network checklist after this.
07:25 Liam: quick ques — competitors: we benchmarked against Anthropic and roadmap includes moving some workloads to Vertex in the future; curious how Redwood compares on token-per-dollar.
07:34 Daniel: we'll include those comps in the quote; Redwood typically gives lower unit cost on reserved + quantization options.
07:40 Priya: thanks that's useful.
07:44 Maya: ok recap: Aquila to send traces & sample prompts (Priya), Daniel to run throughput estimate and plan benchmark (Daniel + Sofia), Maya to prepare reserved capacity quote, security docs and schedule benchmark. we'll aim for POC kickoff next week.
07:58 Priya: yep thanks everyone.
08:00 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the calendar invite and docs. bye.

[End of transcript]
